summary: Edge header encoding transforms tenant principal and causes RBAC lookup failures in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after a network appliance upgrade in their edge stack, users in the private deployment started receiving 403s from Redwood Inference when invoking the admin APIs. Impact: Admin and service accounts for several tenants could not perform operations (role listing, service account impersonation). This blocks customer ops and scheduled model rollouts. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) for AceroHealth, prod/us-west, Redwood identity-proxy v2.3.1, customer-managed HAProxy 2.6.4 that sits in front of the identity proxy. Observed behavior: Requests arriving at identity-proxy contain an X-Forwarded-User header, but the value appears base64-like (e.g., "QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE=") instead of expected email/principal string. Authentication succeeds (JWT validated) but tenant resolution/subject canonicalization fails when mapping header to tenant-scoped principal, causing RBAC to drop all role bindings and return 403. Steps to reproduce: 1) Using a customer edge box with upgraded HAProxy, make a request to admin list roles endpoint with a valid OIDC token. 2) Observe 403. 3) Capture request at identity-proxy; header shows encoded principal. Logs / relevant headers: - Received header: X-Forwarded-User: QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE= - Expected header: X-Forwarded-User: alice.user@acerohealth.com - Example request id: rwd-req-20260310-7a3f - Identity-proxy log snippet (redacted): "tenant resolution failed: canonicalize_subject returned empty after header parse" Expected behavior: identity-proxy should map the incoming principal to a tenant and apply RBAC bindings; requests should not be blocked by a header encoding transformation introduced by the customer's edge appliance. Notes: Customer claims this started immediately after HAProxy upgrade and a config push from their network team. They do not intend to change upstream identity header behavior without a controlled rollout.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: network appliance config is intentionally encoding principal header. Confirmed by customer's HAProxy config and captured header values. Reproduced behavior in an internal testbed with HAProxy configured to base64-encode headers. Root cause: identity-proxy strictly validates header format and uses simple string canonicalization that rejects non-UTF8 or non-email-looking values, resulting in tenant lookup failing and RBAC falling back to deny. Risk assessment: automatically decoding customer-supplied headers can be risky (maliciously crafted values). Implemented temporary conservative decode that only runs when header matches strict base64 regex and decoded value matches tenant principal pattern (email-like). Logged this as INT-4421 for permanent fix: add explicit header-shaping policy and a tenant-trust flag for private deployments.
resolution: Workaround applied: deployed hotfix identity-proxy build that decodes base64-encoded X-Forwarded-User when and only when decoded value matches tenant principal pattern. Customer validated hotfix in canary and then applied to fleet. Permanent remediation: engineering to implement an opt-in header-normalization policy in identity-proxy and update private deployment docs with guidance: (1) do not transform identity headers upstream; (2) if transformation is required, coordinate with Redwood support to enable safe decoding or use signed headers. Follow-ups: INT-4421 (engineer work item), update Confluence runbook, add test coverage for encoded-header handling. Customer action: revert HAProxy base64 header encoding in next maintenance window.
notes_for_followup: 1) Add UI warning in Console when private deployments detect non-canonical identity headers. 2) Create k8s readiness probe for identity-proxy that flags header-normalization mismatches. 3) Add a short KB article for customers describing safe header transformations.
